options.why: Counted only the horizontal and vertical fold lines and omitted both diagonals.
Counted one vertical fold and stopped instead of testing every possible fold line.
Counted the two halves made by each of the four fold lines as separate lines.

questions.solution_text:
The horizontal and vertical midlines and both diagonals are fold lines.
The square has $4$ lines of symmetry.

options.why: Tested folds rather than turns and treated the lack of line symmetry as no rotational symmetry.
Used the number of sides as the rotational order even though the quadrilateral is not regular.
Forgot that every shape matches at a full turn, so rotational order cannot be zero.

questions.solution_text:
The shape matches after a $180^{\circ}$ turn and after a full turn.
Its rotational symmetry is order $2$.

questions.question_text: Which description matches a non-square rectangle?

options.text: $2$ lines of symmetry and rotational order $2$
$4$ lines of symmetry and rotational order $4$
options.why: Used the symmetry properties of a square instead of a non-square rectangle.

options.text: $2$ lines of symmetry and rotational order $4$
options.why: Counted the four vertices as matching turns, although quarter-turns swap the unequal side lengths.

options.text: $0$ lines of symmetry and rotational order $2$
options.why: Used the symmetry properties of a general parallelogram and missed the rectangle's two midline folds.

questions.solution_text:
The two midlines are fold lines, and the rectangle matches after a $180^{\circ}$ turn.
It has $2$ lines of symmetry and rotational order $2$.

questions.question_text: Which quadrilateral has its two diagonals as its only lines of symmetry?

options.why: A rectangle's fold lines join midpoints of opposite sides; its diagonals are not fold lines.
A general parallelogram has no lines of symmetry, even though its diagonals cross at the centre.
A kite has only one diagonal as a line of symmetry, not both diagonals.

questions.solution_text:
Both diagonals of a rhombus divide it into matching reflected halves.
The quadrilateral is a non-square rhombus.

questions.question_text: A quadrilateral has one line of symmetry and rotational symmetry of order $1$. Which shape could it be?

options.why: A square has four lines of symmetry and rotational order four, not one of each.
A rectangle has two lines of symmetry and rotational order two.
A general parallelogram has rotational order two and no lines of symmetry.

questions.solution_text:
A kite folds along one diagonal and does not match again until a full turn.
A kite can have $1$ line of symmetry and rotational order $1$.

questions.question_text: Luca claims that rotational symmetry of order $2$ guarantees at least one line of symmetry. Which counterexample disproves the claim?

options.why: A rectangle has rotational order two, but it also has two lines of symmetry, so it does not disprove the claim.
A rhombus has rotational order two, but it also has two diagonal lines of symmetry.
A square has both line and rotational symmetry, and its rotational order is four rather than two.

questions.solution_text:
A general parallelogram matches after a $180^{\circ}$ turn but no fold line matches its halves.
It is a counterexample.
